summary:
The web rendering architecture holds up. Every (app) page is dynamic and per-user. Reads go through a request-scoped React cache(). Each read is settled into a designed partial-failure state. Dates format in an explicit en-US locale and the project's own timezone, so server and client render the same text. CLS measured 0 on all 30 cold routes. prefetch={false} demonstrably stops speculative fan-out (0 prefetch requests). Nothing here calls for Cache Components, PPR, 'use cache', workers or virtualization.

Highest-impact item, at the edge of this dimension: the web sign-out Server Actions call supabase.auth.signOut() with no scope. auth-js defaults that to 'global', which revokes the person's phone-collector session. The Account page promises the opposite ("Signing out here does not affect the app"). Uploads stop until the person signs in again. Records are not lost. The fix is one argument.

Second: the project and org loading.tsx files mount a new Suspense boundary on every tab switch. React 19.3's 300 ms reveal throttle then holds back pages that are ready in 60 ms. Measured: tab switches become usable at 327-345 ms, versus RSC plus about 20 ms for moves that don't remount the boundary. The user sees an empty card each time.

Third: every map page re-downloads, unzips and projects the whole package per render, and ships the full-resolution plan to client components. A reproducer on the real functions shows this is harmless at pilot size (real survey: 61 KB). It hits a cliff far below the API's 16 MiB ceiling: about 6 MB of plan JSON at an 832 KiB package, and an out-of-memory crash near 8 MiB.

The rest is lower impact:
- The Data table renders every record twice (15,213 DOM nodes, 2.2 MB of HTML for 500 rows).
- Mutations re-render the current page, often twice.
- A few independent reads run one after another.
- zod is bundled on every /o route because of one helper import.
- Compatibility code contradicts the no-legacy policy.

## How a workspace page gets from navigation to usable content (verified in code)

1. **Proxy.** `proxy.ts:13-49` runs on every matched request, including RSC and Server Action POSTs. It calls `getClaims()`, which is local: the project signs ES256 (`docs/Supabase-Setup.md:11`) and auth-js keeps the JWKS cache module-global (`GoTrueClient.js:49-69`). A signed-out request to a protected path redirects to `/sign-in?next=`. Matched responses get `Cache-Control: private, no-store`.
2. **(app) layout.** `(app)/layout.tsx:28` awaits `getWorkspace()`: `session()` (getClaims + getSession), then `GET /v1/me`. It never throws. The whole index goes to `WorkspaceProvider`. This blocks all `(app)` HTML. Measured TTFB is 25-57 ms locally. It is needed for slug-to-ID resolution and roles, so the block is justified.
3. **Org layout and project layout.** `[org]/layout.tsx:20-38` and `p/[project]/layout.tsx:23-26` add cache hits, `notFound()` and the observer redirect. Per the bundled docs (`06-fetching-data.md:455`), layouts and pages render in parallel, so page reads start at the same time.
4. **Page.** Each page runs `resolveProject` (a cache hit), then its own waves of reads. Every read is `settle()`d into a `Result`, and a failed read renders a designed `LoadFailure`, never an empty list.
5. **Hand-off.** Props are serialized to `'use client'` screens, then streamed through the project `loading.tsx` Suspense, then hydrated.

On soft navigations only the changed segments render, but every page still pays one `/v1/me` call (`get_identity` appears in every warm-nav list). Back and forward are served from the router cache in 12-20 ms with no requests.

## Specific questions

- **Does getWorkspace block every child, and what loading/Suspense exists?** Yes, by design. Only two segment loading files exist (project, org) plus Overview's Coverage Suspense. They flush a skeleton on cold loads, but on soft navigations they cost ≥300 ms per tab switch (R2).
- **Archives during render (R3).** Triggered on Overview coverage, Data, observation detail, Sites (×6), Site, Zones, the zone editor and publish, package inspect, the form editor, and `loadSitePlanAction`. Repeated on every navigation. Synchronous unzip on the event loop. Projected JSON is about 6-7× the zip. Fine at pilot scale (real survey: 61 KB); a cliff near 1-8 MiB.
- **Large props.**
  - Data: 500 rows → 418.6 KB RSC and 2.2 MB HTML; most of the HTML is the doubled DOM (R4).
  - Reports: 288 KB HTML for 520 observations.
  - The workspace index and the timezone list are small: there is no evidence they matter.
- **Client graph.**
  - cmdk is about 20 KB raw: keep it eager.
  - Radix is shared by the dialogs.
  - zod (73 KB br) reaches 10 routes only through LoadFailure (R7).
  - supabase-js is needed only when the user clicks export on Data, Site or QGIS.
  - Lazy-loading CommandPalette would only delay the first ⌘K; not worth it.
- **prefetch={false}.** Justified. The overview has 31 workspace links, and measured prefetch requests are 0. With the default ("auto") prefetch, each visible link would still hit the server (proxy, layouts, /v1/me) only to fetch a loading shell, because dynamic data is never prefetched. The navigation latency people feel comes from R2, not from the missing prefetch.
- **revalidatePath breadth.** With `fetch` no-store and no Data Cache, revalidation re-renders the current page and purges the router cache; it invalidates nothing on the server.
  - `/o` layout revalidation after org, team, settings and account changes is correct, because the header and switchers read the workspace index.
  - Revalidating the project layout on every form Save is waste, and three flows refresh twice (R5).
  - No client state is lost: the editor's key is stable and its state comes from initial props.
- **Boundaries.**
  - Every project page sits under `p/[project]/error.tsx`.
  - Org pages sit under `[org]/error.tsx` and `not-found.tsx`.
  - `notFound()` thrown in the project layout lands on the org not-found (the shell stays). Thrown in the org layout, it lands on the root not-found (public header). Acceptable.
  - `/account`, `/o`, `/collect` and the auth pages rely on global-error, but they catch API failures themselves.
  - Latent issue, not a finding: `apiRequestError` (`errors.ts:284-291`) turns any TypeError reaching `settle()` into "DECA Mark cannot be reached". Probing odd archives (scratchpad/repro/odd-package.mjs) found no reachable case.
- **Hydration and theme.**
  - Every formatter fixes `en-US` and an explicit timezone (`lib/time.ts:108-111`, `labels.ts:56`), and `nowIso` comes from the server, so server and client render the same text.
  - `InvitationCard` and `ErrorView` use the browser's timezone, but render only after an action or effect.
  - The head `THEME_SCRIPT` plus `suppressHydrationWarning` on `<html>` gives no flash; CLS was 0.
- **Deep links, refresh, back/forward.**
  - Data filters live in the URL (`router.push`, so Back undoes them); search text via debounced `replaceState` that keeps `history.state`.
  - Reports, QGIS and Overview use `router.replace`.
  - The leave guard copies the router's history entry, so Back is held without breaking the router.
  - Back is served from the router cache. The zone editor re-reads its draft before saving, so a page restored from history cannot overwrite a newer draft.
- **Cache Components / PPR / 'use cache'** (`cacheComponents:false`, `config-shared.js:135`). No justified benefit on any route.
  - Every route is per-user and authorized per request.
  - A static shell would only show empty chrome.
  - Identity is one fast call that must stay fresh for role changes.
  - The only immutable, repeated data is the package plan. The byte guard in R3 is the bounded fix; caching it is premature until real package sizes show a need.

justified_choices: prefetch={false} on workspace links: 0 measured prefetch RSC requests across 31 overview links. It protects the API from per-link proxy plus /v1/me fan-out, and with dynamic routes the default would only have prefetched a loading shell anyway.
One getWorkspace per request through React cache(), and getWorkspace never throws; layouts and pages share one /v1/me call.
settle()/Result with LoadFailure: one failed read renders a designed partial state, and a failed fetch is never an empty list (honesty rule).
Every Intl formatter fixes locale en-US and an explicit project timezone, and nowIso is computed on the server, so SSR and hydration produce identical text.
Head THEME_SCRIPT plus suppressHydrationWarning only on <html>, with data-platform for shortcut hints: no theme flash; CLS 0 on all 30 measured routes.
Overview's Coverage section in its own Suspense, so the package archive does not block the rest of the Overview.
Package uploads, exports and downloads go browser -> API directly (bodies up to 24 MiB) instead of through Server Actions (2 MB limit).
Data view state lives in the URL (router.push per filter, debounced replaceState for search that preserves history.state): deep links, refresh and Back all work.
The observation detail page draws the record's own package version (historical binding), not today's map.
Cache-Control private, no-store and Referrer-Policy no-referrer on all proxied responses; the service worker never stores authenticated responses or RSC payloads.
No Cache Components, PPR or 'use cache': every route is per-user, and nothing measured needs them.
ES256 sign-in with a module-global JWKS cache: getClaims in the proxy and on the server verifies locally, with no auth round trip per request.
not_covered: Form routes (list, versions, editor, publish) were measured only on their failure path: the lab API returned 500 for listForms and getFormVersion, so editor render time and Save latency are unmeasured (this is a backend or lab-database issue, outside this dimension).
No CPU- or network-throttled runs and no hosted Vercel -> Render waterfall; per-wave cost in production is inferred, not measured.
Not measured at all: zone publish, /invite, /join and /o/[org]/collect.
The proposed persistent-Suspense replacement for loading.tsx (R2) is reasoned from the Next layout-router and React source, not run.
The mobile consequence of the web's global sign-out is traced through the mobile inventory map and auth-js source, not run on a device.
Whether Next server-renders error.tsx (ErrorView uses the browser timezone in a useState initializer) was not verified at runtime.
Server memory limits of the hosted function were not checked; the out-of-memory point in R3 comes from a local Node process.

summary:
The data and caching layer is mostly sound. Nothing is cached on the server: API fetches use `no-store`, and React `cache()` only lasts for one request. There is no optimistic UI, so a refresh can never bring old data back. The service worker stores only public files. The WorkspaceProvider sends the viewer only their own data. Manager-only pages check the role before they read, and the database functions I sampled enforce membership and role again. The counts say when they come from the newest 500. Signing out writes cookies inside a Server Action, and in Next 16.2.7 that clears both the client router cache and the back/forward cache. The packagePlans memo is keyed by user, project and package.

There are three material defects, all reachable by ordinary use or a plain phishing link:
(1) The web Sign out uses Supabase's default global scope. It ends the person's collector session on every device, while the Account page says signing out "does not affect the app".
(2) The code assumes every Server Action call resolves to a typed result. A dropped connection, a session that ended (the proxy redirects action POSTs with 307), or a version mismatch after a deploy makes the call reject instead. In the form editor and the settings screens that rejection reaches the error boundary, so the editor unmounts and unsaved form edits are lost behind "Your records remain available". Some other call sites just fail with no message.
(3) `safeNext` checks for "//" before the URL is normalised, so a link like `/sign-in?next=/a/..//evil.com` sends the person to an outside site right after a real sign-in. I reproduced this with the real function.

Two low findings complete the list. The installed web app shows the marketing page offline. Browser-direct uploads and exports, and the palette's recent places, ignore which account the tab belongs to. All fixes are a few lines each. Nothing here calls for adding caching.

## Identity / caching risks
1. **Global sign-out (WDI-2):** web Sign out and "Not you?" end the person's sessions on every device, including the collector; the Account page copy says otherwise.
2. **Ended session or dropped connection during a Server Action (WDI-1):** the proxy 307s action POSTs. Rejected actions are not caught in transitions, so unsaved form-editor and settings input is lost behind a generic error.
3. **Open redirect (WDI-3):** `safeNext` returns `//host` for paths that normalise to it. This is the only external-navigation hole found.
4. **Account binding (WDI-5):** only the zone editor and account deletion check that the signed-in account is the page's. Upload, import, export and downloads, plus the palette recents, do not.
5. **Stale shell after another manager changes your role:** `WorkspaceProvider` and the project tabs are layout state and are not refetched on soft navigation. This affects controls only; every page and every API call re-checks. Acceptable.
6. **Back button after sign-out:** safe in Next 16.2.7, because cookie writes in the sign-out action purge the router's back/forward cache and documents are `private, no-store`.
7. **Service worker:** nothing authenticated is cached. The offline `/o` fallback to the marketing page is misleading, not harmful (WDI-4). The legacy `fieldmaps-*` cache names are pre-launch compatibility code and can be deleted.
8. **Caching research data:** do not add any. If plan projection cost is ever addressed, the only safe server memo key is an immutable package id, used after the user's own authorised package read. Measure first.

justified_choices: No server data cache: API fetches use cache:'no-store' (web/src/lib/api/client.ts:57) and React cache() only removes duplicate reads within one request (lib/api/workspace.ts:55-62). No 'use cache', unstable_cache or staleTimes anywhere. For authenticated research data this is the right default, and it means a refresh always shows the API's current state.

Sign-out and sign-in run as Server Actions that write cookies. In Next 16.2.7 any cookie set/delete in an action marks ActionDidRevalidateStaticAndDynamic (server/web/spec-extension/adapters/request-cookies.js:111-116), and the client then calls invalidateBfCache and invalidateEntirePrefetchCache (server-action-reducer.js:192-209; docs 01-app/04-glossary.md:45). So Back after sign-out refetches and the proxy redirects; documents are also private, no-store (proxy.ts:47).

The WorkspaceProvider index holds only the viewer's own userId, name, email and their orgs, projects and roles (lib/workspace/types.ts:27-52, build.ts:37-63); no other members, no join codes, no tokens.

Invitation secrets: lists never carry them (backend invitation_schemas.py:42-59; token and code only on InvitationCreated, shown once). The link secret lives in the URL fragment, then in this tab's sessionStorage, and is removed from the address bar (features/auth/InviteScreen.tsx:76-85); no-referrer is set on the proxy response and on the invite and join pages.

Pages check the role before reading: Members, Org settings, Team, Project settings and Form publish all check abilities before calling manager-only endpoints (e.g. team/page.tsx:32-49, (org)/members/page.tsx:24-32). The API/DB enforces this again for client-supplied ids: change_org_member, change_project_member and create_invitation check has_org_role/has_project_role (supabase baseline.sql:300-336,467-490), and require_manager is used in services/tenancy.py:53,59 and services/invitations.py:132,137.

packagePlans memo is keyed userId:projectId:packageId over immutable packages (features/data/plans.ts:3-17), so sign-out or an account change cannot leak a plan; DataMap ignores late responses with a request token (DataMap.tsx:119-187).

summary:
The collector gets the hard parts right. A save is one transaction. The upload body is frozen when the record is saved and re-sent with the same id after a lost response. A record is marked "Uploaded" only after the server's receipt matches it. Rejected records stay put and show a safe reason. Accounts are kept apart, and late async work is discarded after an account change. What breaks the "never lose a record" promise is how the app handles its own updates and two things it says.

1. Any SCHEMA_VERSION mismatch silently wipes every unsent observation, draft and package file before any screen appears. I reproduced it with the real code. The version was bumped twice in the week the pilot user started.
2. The Account, Sign-out and Delete-account screens tell observers the app "does not upload yet". Delete-account says it "cannot upload them first". So observers make data-losing choices at exactly the moments that matter.
3. Saved rows are re-checked against the current strict schema, one failure takes the whole read down, and the only error message is shown on a screen observers don't see. One bad row can block every map, hide all parked drafts or stop all uploads, and nothing explains why.
4. Retry delays carry over into the next foreground session. Since uploads only happen while the app is open, the observer can sit on Wi-Fi watching nothing happen for up to 5 minutes.
5. Every token refresh rebuilds the map-package machinery. That silently cancels downloads, briefly shows maps on the device as "Not downloaded", and re-verifies every package on the JS thread.
6. An idle 5-second timer bumps a counter that makes every open screen re-read the whole observations table. The Account counts and the Sign-out button flicker, and the field map is rebuilt.

The fixes are small. Most of them delete code: the "legacy" scope, the transition paths and the tables nothing reads. None needs a migration.

## Shell shown vs ready to collect (cold start)

1. **Fonts**: Splash "Opening DECA Mark".
2. **SQLiteProvider `onInit`** (behind Suspense): `user_version` check and WAL. On a mismatch, a full reset and `hosted/` deletion happen here, before any UI exists.
3. **AuthProvider `createAuthClient`**: staging and production builds read the legacy keychain entry; `last-account.json` and the deleted-account marker are read synchronously. "Opening your workspace" shows until `ready`, which is set with `session=null` and the cached account.
4. **Children mount**: MeProvider reads `me.json` synchronously; HostedSitesProvider runs `reconcileStaging` and catalog run #1 (api null); draft and parked recovery reads start. GatedStack holds a splash only when there is no local profile and `/v1/me` has not settled. **The shell is shown here.** No live session is needed; collecting works offline with a cached account.
5. **INITIAL_SESSION** arrives with a new session object. `/v1/me` is re-fetched. HostedSites `api` and `operations` are recreated, run #1 is discarded after its current package, and catalog run #2 re-reads, hashes and zod-validates every retained version on the JS thread. Until it lands, `installed=[]` and sites say "Not downloaded".
6. **TOKEN_REFRESHED** (online, expired token): run #3, plus `/v1/me` and `/sites` for every project again.
7. **Ready to collect**: the package is verified in `installed`, then Projects → Site "Set up this session" (`openPackage`, refused while an unreadable or other draft holds the slot) → Brief "Start collection" (blocked only by a resumable draft) → `/collect` (`beginVisit` takes the lease).

## Outbox vocabulary (stored state vs screens)

| Stored | Account / tab badge (`queue.ts`) | Observations tab (`records.tsx`) | Contract (`contour.json` / DESIGN) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `local-only` | Held | On device only | Held = waiting on the project |
| `pending` | On device | **Held** ("held for signal") | On device |
| (none) | Uploading (always 0) | — | Uploading = being sent now (never produced) |
| `synced` | Uploaded | **Synced** | Uploaded (never "Synced") |
| `needs-attention` | Needs attention | Needs attention | Needs attention |

"Uploaded" is never shown before a matching receipt; that part is honest.

## Account switching, privacy, membership

- **Partitioning.** Everything is keyed by `owner_scope`, and every token use checks `session.user.id === scope.userId`. The next account cannot list, open or upload the previous account's rows. Generation fences (session `current()`, sync `current()`, HostedSites epoch, `useObservations` generation) discard late async work. No listener, timer, location-watch or DB leak was found.
- **Welcome screen.** It shows other signed-out accounts' email and unsent and draft counts on a shared tablet. No record content is shown. This is acceptable for the product's "clear owner" rule; it is a disclosure of colleagues' emails only.
- **Retention.** Deleted accounts' records and all package bytes stay on the device indefinitely (`removeAccountData` has no caller; removal never deletes files). The delete-account copy says records stay, which is honest, but its "cannot upload them first" is false (MOB-REC-02).
- **At rest.** SQLite (answers, coordinates, observer initials), `me.json` (email, name, memberships) and package JSON are plaintext in `Documents/` (expo-sqlite uses `Documents/SQLite`; no backup exclusion found). They are protected by OS sandboxing and data protection, and included in device backups. The session is AES-GCM-encrypted with the key in SecureStore. This is not a finding: record it in the privacy page and IRB notes rather than encrypting the DB now.
- **Membership removed while records are queued.** There is no client-side gate. The server answers `membership_required`, the record goes to needs-attention with "You are no longer a member of this project. Contact its manager.", it stays on the device and can be retried after re-adding. Installed packages get the `no_access` problem; open, resume and download are refused. This is correct.
- **Package removal while referenced.** It is refused for any lease, draft or record, including synced records, so a map ever used can never be removed. No record risk.

## Concrete rerender chains

- **5 s tick.** `SyncProvider.setRevision` → (a) every focused `useObservations` (full-table read, `loading` flip) → `CollectScreen` → `CollectMap` new GeoJSON; (b) `FieldSessionProvider` (consumes `useSync`) → new context value → every `useFieldSession` consumer; (c) `useSiteVersions` re-queries on mounted Site and Brief screens.
- **Token refresh.** `AuthProvider` new session → `MeProvider` effect (re-fetch, new `projects`) → site discovery reset and re-fetch; HostedSites `api` → `operations` → dispose (downloads aborted), `installed=[]`, catalog re-verify; Sync effect rebuild (aborts the in-flight PUT, harmless because it is idempotent).
- **Location on.** About 1 Hz `set()` → `CollectMap` re-render (by design, limited to the map).

summary:
Maps, forms and package handling are mostly well built. Records freeze their package, zone and form at first placement. Recovery refuses to substitute a different package. Placement and save use the same exact closed-coverage predicate as the server. The web Data table, map and export follow the same filters, and the export says plainly that the search is not applied. None of the problems found loses a record.

The defects that matter are elsewhere. First, on Android the Collect answer panel has no keyboard avoidance (`behavior={undefined}`), even though the build is edge-to-edge and the project's own Screen.tsx comment says the window does not resize. Janet's inventory form has 8 text questions, so on the pilot Android tablet observers would type into a field the keyboard covers. Second, every token refresh rebuilds PackageOperations. That silently aborts any package download in flight, which is most likely right after resuming a stale app, and re-verifies every installed package. Third, the 5-second sync tick bumps `revision` even when nothing changed. Every focused screen then re-reads and zod-parses every record the device has ever kept. The Observations header flickers, and the Collect map re-serializes the whole package to JSON.

The other costs are real but grow with data size, and none is measured on a device. Records are never pruned and the Observations list is a plain ScrollView. The map re-stringifies the package on every render, which today is about 9 KB and costs nothing. Package install keeps about six whole-package copies, and the catalog runs again on every start. The web Data page renders each record twice (measured: 15,213 DOM nodes and 2.27 MB of HTML for 500 records). The web server re-downloads immutable archives on every plan view. On bundles, no map, editor or archive library loads where it shouldn't on either platform. The fixes are small: change a prop, change a dependency, add a guard on a callback, add a WHERE/LIMIT, pre-stringify once. None needs a new library, a worker, clustering or a different map engine.

justified_choices: Web plans are hand-written SVG (SitePlan/MapFrame) rather than a GL or tile map library: there is no map dependency in any bundle, 500 markers and 250 zones are within SVG's comfortable range, camera moves are batched per rAF and the background layer is memoized.
Mobile keeps MapLibre mounted across Place, Answer, Review and Saved, with an imperative camera (initialViewState plus easeTo/fitBounds), so there is no controlled-camera render loop.
Mobile draws prior observations as GPU circle layers with property-driven selection, and clusters with an O(n log n) grid only below zoom 18. That is enough without a clustering library.
The aim store is throttled to 100 ms, and the placement readout (useAimZone) and CandidateEdges are isolated so the map itself does not re-render on camera events.
Placement gating, the save re-check and zone taps all use the same exact closed-coverage predicate (zoneCovers) as the server, so the device and the server agree about edge points.

The form engine is pure and data-driven (conditions are data, there is pruning with a 'dropped' notice, and validation happens only at review). It is easy to test and matches the backend engine's semantics.
Drafts are written on every keystroke through serialized SQLite transactions, deliberately without debouncing so a force quit loses nothing; the cost is one small row.

Records and drafts freeze the package, zone and form binding at first placement, and recovery refuses substitution. The web observation detail and the Data map honour the version each record was collected on.
Web Data keeps the table, map, counts and export consistent, and states honestly what each one covers (the subset note, the search-not-applied note).
SHA-256 runs through expo-crypto's native digest rather than a JS implementation.
Web keeps a small per-account LRU of site plans (packagePlans, 8 entries) so switching versions on the Data map does not re-fetch.
Zone editor drags are batched per rAF, and problems are computed on settled zones, not on every frame.

summary: The pattern across this codebase is not too much abstraction. The policy is applied in the wrong place. The owner's "resets are fine" rule protects development databases, but the collector applies it to the observer's phone. initializeDatabase drops every SQLite table, unsent records and drafts included, whenever SCHEMA_VERSION changes. That happened twice in three days (5 on 10-11, 6 on 10-13), and nothing is counted or warned about first. The same missing non-destructive path is why a frozen "legacy" owner_scope stays the account key: three of its four fields are constants (127.0.0.1:8000, the hosted issuer and a fixed project), and issuer checks compare one constant with another. Changing the key today would orphan every pending row. Next by impact is the release Observations tab. It is still the pre-Contour (Nocturne) records screen, with its own status words: pending shows as "Held" and synced as "Synced", against PRODUCT.md's vocabulary. That screen also drags about 1 MB of Inter fonts in front of the first frame. The duplicated rules are mostly deliberate and fairly cheap: a byte-copied form engine, per-platform primitives over one token contract, and error tables checked against the generated ErrorCode type. But the guards that make the copies safe do not run: forms:parity, the web unit tests (393) and tokens:check are absent from CI, while the docs present them as checks. Web also keeps a fourth, unguarded form model (answers.ts) that exists mainly for the legacy `fields` format, which the backend dropped in 577959a. Leftovers from the rename (11 redirects, old service-worker cache names, the fieldmaps:// scheme, the SecureStore migration) and several write-only mobile tables can go without losing any guarantee. The security boundaries hold up. In particular, the reported safeNext open redirect cannot be reached end to end, because the sign-in action applies safeNext again and refuses "//host". Change cost is moderate. The worst traps are (1) a strict filter schema in Data's server action that TypeScript does not tie to ObservationFilters, (2) question-kind renderers written as if-chains that compile when a kind is missing, and (3) LAYER_NAMES declared in five places.

## Claims checked and rejected
- **The safeNext open redirect (web-data-identity F3) cannot be reached.** The page's safeNext turns "/a/..//evil" into "//evil" for the hidden input. But lib/auth/actions.ts:41 (authenticate) and features/auth/actions.ts:125 (switchAccount) call safeNext(form.get("next")) again, and "//evil" fails the startsWith("//") check, so the result is "/o". Reproduced in scratchpad/repro/simp/safenext.mjs. No client code calls router.push(next). What remains: safeNext is not idempotent, so a future direct redirect of the page-level value would open the hole. A two-line origin check fixes that.
- **Zod in web client bundles.** The zod/openapi-fetch chunk (391 KB raw, 90.7 KB gzip, static-bundle.json) loads on every /o route (cold.json). One path is LoadFailure, which imports isNoAccess from lib/workspace/result.ts, which imports zod through lib/api/errors.ts. But 13 other client modules legitimately pull zod-bearing libraries, so moving isNoAccess saves bytes only on routes without them. The benefit is unmeasured; this is not reported as a finding.
- **Sampled comments that claim guarantees.** "One transaction: a record can never be stored while its draft survives" (session/observation-actions.ts:189) holds: observation-store.ts:63-77 inserts the record and deletes the draft in one databaseTransaction. The false guarantee lives in the docs instead: PRODUCT.md promises no record loss (S1), and AGENTS.md:20 describes tokens:check as enforcing (S3).

summary:
The web manager workspace is mostly honest and careful. Counts say when they are capped ("Showing 1–500 of 520 · counted at 12:14"), dates carry the project time zone, unbuilt features get a NotAvailable note instead of a fake button, and the export dialog repeats its scope, says the search is not applied and refuses more than 10,000 records. For one site, the site page answers "what does an observer download right now?" correctly: package version, form version and inventory form.

The problems sit where the manager has to connect separate objects: a QGIS export, a form version, a map package and an observer.

1. **Misleading upload error.** When the server blocks a map upload during package preparation, the reason is discarded. The manager is told a zone's rings are malformed. This happens with any QGIS project that has an online basemap, and the lab's real Ithaca project does.
2. **No way to tell which form observers use.** The Forms list pairs the newest published version with sites that actually use an older one. Overview then says "Nothing needs attention." Publishing a form never reaches observers until the whole QGIS export is uploaded again. That re-upload asks the manager to confirm each zone one at a time, and it silently replaces any boundaries edited on the web.
3. **Data map out of reach on iPad.** Below 1280 px (every iPad and many laptops) the site plan is drawn after up to 500 table rows. This contradicts DESIGN.md's 768 px rule.
4. **Invitations.** The join code and link are shown once, and pressing Esc or tapping the dim background closes that dialog and loses them. Invitation emails that fail are never reported.
5. **Smaller defects.**
   - The observer filter is case-sensitive, so typing lowercase initials says nothing matches.
   - Returning from an observation via the "Data" breadcrumb drops the filters.
   - In an empty project, the one highlighted button points at an empty Data page.

The web code is identical between the audited commit 9928f53 and the current HEAD b93a2b2. Nothing was rendered at tablet widths, so the iPad layout and upload-feedback claims come from reading the code and CSS.

## Novice vs experienced (heuristic)
- **Novice manager:**
  - The setup order loops: package → form → package.
  - Two QGIS project inputs with different meanings, and red "Fails" badges before anything is chosen.
  - Terms like "Inventory form" and "Which zone is each zone in the file?".
  - The invite hint suggests a multi-use code but the default is 1.
  - The misleading upload error (UXW-1) is the worst trap.
- **Experienced manager:**
  - Repeated work on every form revision: re-upload and re-confirm every zone (UXW-4).
  - Lost filters on return from a record (UXW-7).
  - Exact-case observer filter (UXW-6).
  - On iPad, no usable map (UXW-3).
- **Both:**
  - Inconsistent answers to "which form are observers on?" (UXW-2).

## Current vs proposed interactions

**1. Getting a corrected form to observers**
- Current: Forms → editor → Save → Publish → tick the box → Publish play-v2 → toast → versions list → (manager must remember) Sites → Fall Creek → Upload a new version → choose .qgz + sources → Read project → check Form version = play-v2 → for each of N zones pick "Same zone as …" → Upload package → (if the zones were edited on the web, the boundaries silently revert). Meanwhile the Forms list shows "Published play-v2 · Used by Fall Creek" and Overview shows "Nothing needs attention".
- Proposed: Forms → editor → Save → Publish → tick the box → Publish play-v2. The publish result lists "Fall Creek uses play-v1 — [Use play-v2 on Fall Creek's map]", which publishes map vN+1 from the current archive with play-v2. Until that is done, Overview shows a waiting item "play-v2 is published; no site's map names it", and the Forms list reads "Fall Creek · play-v1".

**2. Uploading a real QGIS project that has a basemap**
- Current: choose .qgz + gpkg → Read project ("N layers read… Imagery and QGIS styling are not imported.") → Upload package → "Not uploaded. A zone's shape could not be read. Check that each of its rings is closed…". The manager edits zones in QGIS, re-exports and gets the same error.
- Proposed: Read project lists "Basemap 'OpenStreetMap' (tile service) will block the package: remove it from the project, or upload without the project file". If the manager uploads anyway: "Not uploaded. Imagery licence: OpenStreetMap (tile.openstreetmap.org) is fetched from a tile service on demand… Remove the layer or supply institution-owned imagery."

**3. Reviewing a filtered set on an iPad**
- Current: Data → set Site, Round and Observer (initials must be uppercase) → table of up to 500 rows, with the plan after the last row → tap a row (nothing visible changes) → open record → "Data" breadcrumb → filters gone.
- Proposed: Data → set filters (initials are uppercased) → the plan sits above the table (compact), or beside it at xl as a sticky panel → tapping a row highlights the point in view → open record → "Data" breadcrumb returns to the same filtered URL.

## The "one magenta action per screen" rule
- Helps on: Site (Upload a new version), Upload (Upload package), Publish (Publish vN), Team (Invite), Data (Export) and Reports (Print).
- Obstructs on Overview for an empty project (UXW-8): the static primary points away from setup.
- No screen shows two primaries in code; the honesty e2e scans for this (`web/e2e/support/scan.ts`).

## Voice and copy
- No "successfully", "Oops", Synced/Pending/Failed labels or bare OK/Submit were found in `web/src`.
- Implementation vocabulary leaks in a few places: "Revision" on the observation detail, and the History "Forms" column shows two unlabelled codes that wrap mid-code (packages-upload.png).
- The doc conflict PRODUCT.md:55 J1 (packages before forms) contradicts the code's prerequisite.

summary:
The collector is careful work. Placement uses a fixed cross with tap-to-jump, 0.5 m nudges and zoom-to-place, plus a live in-zone readout. Recovery reopens the exact map and zone. The download size comes from the server and is checked against the bytes received. "Ready offline" means a re-hashed, verified install. Sign-up and join are short. The flaws are in what the observer sees and touches on a real device, and they cluster in three places.

First, the C3 loop has defects that cost data quality or block a task. On an iPhone, the required multi-line play-event summary is typed blind: the keyboard covers the whole answer panel, and there is no key to dismiss it. A double tap on an auto-advancing answer either clears the answer just given or silently answers the next question; a pure reproduction against janet-test-v1 shows both outcomes. When a draft write fails, the observer is not told, while the Collect status line keeps saying "Draft kept on this device as you answer". If a draft cannot be read, collection is blocked with no card offering a way out.

Second, C4 status words are false where decisions are made. Account and Sign out both say "This version does not upload yet", but uploading is live and signing out pauses it. The Observations tab swaps the whole app for the legacy dark records screen (an operator-verified tablet screenshot shows it). That screen labels waiting records "Held" and uploaded ones "Synced", and its Retry re-sends the same frozen body.

Third, phone layouts were sized for tablets. Map controls are clipped, and the Saved step's only forward action sits below the fold. Separately, in C2, a token refresh silently cancels a running download and briefly shows a downloaded site as "Not downloaded".

Most fixes are small, and several mostly delete code (copy, legacy screen, deps). Nothing here needs a new library or architecture.

summary:
Both frontends are unusually well built for accessibility. The web Contour primitives wire labels, aria-invalid and aria-describedby once, announce messages through live regions, and restore focus through Radix. They also provide a skip link, route focus, a keyboard-complete zone editor with numeric alternatives, a roving-row table with real links, and a global reduced-motion rule. The native primitives carry roles, state, 48 to 60 pt targets, text-scale caps, Reanimated reduce-motion guards, an announce helper, and a non-gesture placement path (nudge buttons plus "Place point here"). I found no contrast defect after recomputing the full token cross-product, both map palettes and the legacy Nocturne palette. Nothing I found risks record loss.

The material problems sit where the design system stops. First, the release Observations tab is the legacy Nocturne screen, with no heading, 5 stops per record, an 11.5 pt text-only state chip and truncation. Second, the accessibility preferences PRODUCT.md promises (Dusk, larger question text, preferred hand, haptics) can only be changed in dev screens. Third, three native live regions are Android-only, so VoiceOver hears nothing when the cross leaves its zone, while two other places announce twice. Fourth, the native map camera ignores Reduce Motion despite the product's own promise.

Web has three low items. The `g`, `/` and `?` keys violate WCAG 2.1.4. The shortcut dialog documents Approve and Exclude keys that do nothing. The password toggles fail Label in Name.

No axe, keyboard or screen-reader output exists in outputs (the journeys directory is absent). Every spoken-output claim here is code-derived. PLAN.md still lists MOB-18 as todo and the VoiceOver passes as pending, so the largest risk to the pilot is the assistive-technology matrix nobody has run.

justified_choices: Accessibility is built once in the primitives. Contour Field supplies htmlFor, aria-invalid and aria-describedby; Button, IconButton, Switch and Checkbox keep 44 px targets via ::before; Note, Field and the zone editor expose live regions. Screens inherit this, which is why page-level axe plus focused specs is enough.
Radix for Dialog, Menu, Popover, Toast, Tooltip, Checkbox, Switch, RadioGroup and ToggleGroup is the right call. Hand-rolling focus trap, restore and typeahead would be the larger risk.
InkTabs is a nav of links with aria-current, not role=tab. That is the correct pattern for route navigation.
Tables use one tab stop with roving rows, tabIndex -1 on the in-row link, and a real OBS link for screen-reader users (DataTable, useRovingRows, Tr).

The zone editor has non-drag equivalents everywhere: arrow keys on handles, bracket keys, I to insert, a numeric PointsTable, and click-click drawing. This satisfies 2.1.1 and 2.5.7. Midpoint handles are drag-only and aria-hidden, with a keyboard alternative.
Coverage and chart graphics always sit with text: CoverageDots has sr text, CountBars and TypeBars show counts, and the Overview coverage map is a hover aid over a focus-linked table.
Web reduced motion is one global CSS rule, and the map camera uses CSS transitions, so no per-component JS check is needed.
Native has a non-gesture placement path: tap-to-aim, four nudge buttons, a move-to-my-location button and "Place point here" using the map's exact centre, with a live coordinate and zone readout.
Native text uses maxFontSizeMultiplier caps of 1.6, 1.8 or 2 depending on role, and controls use minHeight rather than fixed height. That meets 200 percent resize without letting layouts break.
Native question flow moves screen-reader focus to each question heading on mount (QuestionHeading) and announces place, zone-change and save through one announce helper.
Auth forms allow paste and password managers, use one-time-code autocomplete and noValidate with their own inline errors, and focus the first invalid field. That satisfies 3.3.8 and 1.3.5.

Contrast is enforced from one contract (contracts/contour.json) for both apps. I recomputed the full token cross-product, both map palettes and the legacy Nocturne palette: no pair that is actually used fails. The only sub-4.5 cell is Day attention on ledge (4.40), and ledge is a shadow or hover fill that is never a text background.
Opacity is used only for disabled controls on web, which WCAG exempts; no text is dimmed with an opacity modifier.
not_covered: Runtime assistive-technology output: no VoiceOver, TalkBack, NVDA, JAWS or Voice Control run exists, and the journeys, e2e and native evidence directories are absent. Every spoken-output statement here is derived from code and installed framework sources.
Axe results: web/e2e honesty scans and the zones specimen runs were not executed. Their configuration was read, not their output.
Hardware-keyboard, Full Keyboard Access and Switch Control behaviour on native; only TextInput draws a focus ring.
Forced-colors or Windows High Contrast on web (no forced-colors rules exist, and sliding-pill backgrounds would vanish) and OS Increase Contrast or Bold Text on native.
Actual 320 px reflow, 1.4.12 text-spacing overrides, 400 percent zoom, and 200 percent dynamic type clipping on native; only code-level fixed-height checks were done.
VoiceOver and TalkBack reading order on the collect screen, MapLibre's own accessibility tree, and whether the Map accessibilityLabel prop reaches the native view.
Legal and marketing page content, the OTP and invitation email templates, printed or PDF report accessibility, and QGIS outputs.
The generated mobile/ios and mobile/android projects, and native dev galleries (dev-only).
The designs that PLAN.md says are not committed, so design-versus-build comparisons were not made.

summary:
The suites are better than their wiring. Where tests exist they are mostly real: web unit tests import the actual modules and distinguish failure, stale, offline, conflict (412/409/428/429/401) and DST cases; mobile store, outbox and session tests run real SQL (node:sqlite) with fakes only at the network edge; the zone e2e specs exercise two-actor, offline, sign-out-in-another-tab and account-swap journeys. The problem is reach, not quality.

CI runs 84 of 477 web node tests. The 393-test unit suite (2 s) is not run, nor is forms:parity (the only thing tying web's copy of the form engine to the cases that test it) or tokens:check, while docs say CI runs "the same checks". The one test that drives the real collector upload code against the real API has a Python driver that no script, CI job or pytest path invokes; the other four acceptance files skip silently. There is no native runner (MOB-21 is still todo) and mobile component tests render a hand-written fake react-native, so kill-and-relaunch, device upload and the collect screens (CollectScreen, CollectMap, QuestionStep) have no runtime coverage. The schema-reset test asserts that unsent records are wiped; nothing asserts a guard.

The browser suite is cheaper than feared (about 2 min per project for the scan, measured from artifact timestamps), but its "honesty" scan is a copy and layout lint on one seeded success state, screenshots.spec is an asset generator running in five projects, and a handful of tests mirror other tests or pin unreachable compat. Fixes are small: three CI lines, one named command, about ten deletions, four to six new tests. No new framework except Maestro, which the plan already names.

3. **Schema bump with unsent work refuses.** Scenario: DB at SCHEMA_VERSION minus 1 holding one pending, one needs-attention row and an open draft; initializeDatabase rejects with a typed error and all rows remain; with only synced rows it resets. 5. **Account switch with an unsent record on one phone.** Scenario: account A saves a record offline, signs out (warning names the count), account B signs in; B's list is empty and a drain with B's token sends nothing; A signs back in and the record uploads once. keep_despite_complex.item: scripts/*.test.mjs and database/*.test.mjs seed guards
keep_despite_complex.why: Small, in CI, and they prevent the catastrophic misuse of seeding or testing against hosted services.

justified_choices: Store, outbox and session tests run real SQL through node:sqlite behind a thin LocalDatabase adapter and fake only the network edge (mobile/src/storage/package-store.fixture.ts, sync/coordinator.test.ts): this is why lost-response replay, account fences at token/response/queued-write phases and 27-record drains are trustworthy.

Language-neutral contract cases (contracts/forms/definition.cases.json, forms/cases/*.cases.json, zones/geometry.cases.json) are consumed by web, mobile and backend, so one authored expectation guards three implementations.

Web unit tests use node:test with --experimental-strip-types and a 40-line resolve hook (tests/unit/support.mjs): no transpiler, 393 tests in about 2 s, and they execute real src modules rather than copies.

Web unit tests distinguish the states the product promises: 401 pause, 403/404 no access, 412/409/428 conflicts, 429 Retry-After, offline then confirm-on-reconnect, server echo mismatch, unreadable sources not reported as fine, DST fall-back days, counts exact vs capped.

The zone e2e specs (zones-conflict, zones-account, zones-network, zones-publish) test the actual interrupted-work paths against the real API: two managers, sign-out in a second tab, account swap sending nothing for 12 s, offline edit saved on reconnect with a leave guard, lost answer replayed once.

The specimen suite exercises keyboard, mouse and touch geometry editing, lossless serialisation, no tile requests and axe while drawing without needing sign-in or an API; gate 8 attaches frame timings instead of asserting a flaky threshold.
screen.fixture reads controls by accessibility label and text as a screen reader would, and the fixture header states honestly that layout is not computed.

Playwright is configured conservatively: workers 1, retries 0, forbidOnly in CI, loopback-only baseURL guard, and the seed refuses hosted or credential-bearing targets with tests in CI (database/seed-web-workspace.test.mjs, scripts/e2e-local-seed.test.mjs).
tsc includes e2e/*.ts and playwright configs (tsconfig include **/*.ts), eslint covers tests, and biome plus tsc cover mobile tests, so spec code cannot rot at type level.
The service-worker test runs the shipped source in node:vm with fake caches and asserts private URLs, RSC requests and no-store responses are never cached.
not_covered: No test, build or server was run (read-only audit). Pass counts and timings come from outputs/frontend-audit-2026-10-17/checks and mobile-checks. The full Playwright suite was not run for this audit; only a 14-test sign-in run (perf/stackA-e2e-local.log) and Oct 13 artifact mtimes (web/e2e/screenshots, assets/screenshots/web/raw) were available, so functional e2e wall time and flakiness are unmeasured.
Repo HEAD during the audit is b93a2b2 (three commits after the stated 9928f53); findings were verified against the working tree, which matches the clean-tree premise.
web/e2e/.auth/*, .env files, mobile/credentials and database/.local were not opened.
backend/tests (93 files) and database/tests/*.sql were not assessed for quality, only for whether CI reaches them and which driver scripts call them.
No physical device or simulator was driven; native behaviour (expo-sqlite kill semantics, MapLibre, SecureStore) is inferred from sources and fakes.
Whether any current web page swallows a failed read into an empty list was not exhaustively traced (TEST-05 is a missing guard, not a confirmed violation).
Bundle, render and API performance were out of this dimension (other auditors own them).
